name: Giotto
first: ESA's first deep-space mission; closest comet flyby ever attempted (Halley, 596 km, 1986); first close-up imaging of a cometary nucleus
description: Giotto was Europe's pillar of the Halley armada — a spin-stabilised 960 kg probe wrapped in a layered Whipple-Kevlar dust shield. Launched 1985-07-02, it flew through Halley's coma at 68 km/s relative velocity on 1986-03-14 with closest approach 596 km, returning the first close-up images of any cometary nucleus (an irregular 15×8×8 km elongated body with concentrated dust jets). A dust impact 14 seconds before closest approach destabilised the spin axis and killed the camera, but the other instruments kept transmitting through the coma. After hibernating in heliocentric orbit, Giotto reactivated 1990 + used Earth gravity assist to retarget to comet 26P/Grigg-Skjellerup, flying past it at 200 km on 1992-07-10 — the closest cometary flyby ever performed.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: Ariane 1 lifts Giotto from Kourou — ESA's first deep-space mission.

events.label: HALLEY FLYBY
events.note: 596 km closest approach to comet 1P/Halley; first close-up imagery of a cometary nucleus.

events.label: EARTH FLYBY
events.note: Earth gravity assist retargets Giotto to comet 26P/Grigg-Skjellerup.

events.label: GRIGG-SKJELLERUP FLYBY
events.note: 200 km closest approach — the closest cometary flyby on record.
